title: Disjoint rectangles from opposite Bob branches
statement: Let $p$ and $q$ be deterministic two-party protocols, let $A\subseteq X$ and $B\subseteq Y$, and let $f:Y\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$. For distinct bits $b,b'$, any rectangle in the collection of leaf rectangles of $p$ relative to $A$ and the inputs in $B$ where $f(y)=b$ is disjoint from any rectangle in the corresponding collection for $q$ where $f(y)=b'$.
hypotheses_covered: $R$ is a leaf rectangle of $p$ relative to $A$ and $B\cap\{y:f(y)=b\}$
$S$ is a leaf rectangle of $q$ relative to $A$ and $B\cap\{y:f(y)=b'\}$
replaced:
Let $p, q$ be protocols on $X \times Y$, let $A \subseteq X$, $B \subseteq Y$, let
$f : Y \to \{0,1\}$, and let $b \neq b'$ be distinct bits. If $R$ is a leaf rectangle of
$p$ on $A \times (B \cap \{y \mid f(y) = b\})$ and $S$ is a leaf rectangle of $q$ on
$A \times (B \cap \{y \mid f(y) = b'\})$, then $R$ and $S$ are disjoint. This is the
mirror image of \texttt{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.aux\_disjoint\_alice\_of\_ne}.
